production.waterSource: Spring water rises from granite on the slopes of Ben Rinnes above the distillery.
production.malt: Malted barley, spring water and yeast are the only raw production inputs stated by the distillery.
production.stills: The spirit is double-distilled in traditional direct-fired copper pot stills; Glenfarclas continues to emphasise direct firing as a defining production method.
production.maturation: European oak casks previously seasoned with Oloroso sherry are a cornerstone of maturation, selected from a family-run bodega in Spain. Traditional dunnage warehousing remains part of the maturation environment.

houseCharacter: Direct-fired distillation applies intense heat to the still base and contributes to the robust, weighty new-make style Glenfarclas deliberately preserves. Granite-filtered Ben Rinnes spring water supports a clean production base without adding a separate flavour claim beyond its mineral context. Long maturation in Oloroso-seasoned European oak then builds the distillery's familiar combination of sherry richness, spice, dried fruit and substantial texture.
cask23Narrative: Glenfarclas is one of the clearest examples of a distillery protecting an old production choice because it shapes the spirit: the stills remain direct fired. That robust new make is then matured extensively in Oloroso-seasoned European oak, giving the whisky enough structure to carry deep sherry fruit, spice and weight over long ageing. It is a useful dram for understanding how distillation intensity and sherry-cask maturation can be designed to work together rather than independently.
